internal_refs.relationship: Same discriminatory act often triggers both §132a (WCAB) and FEHA §12940(h) (Superior Court) — must pursue both concurrently; different forums, different SOLs
If worker's workers comp claim disclosed employer safety violations, §1102.5 whistleblower protection may overlay §132a retaliation
§132a retaliation presupposes a workers comp claim — occupational injury must first be established

external_refs.relationship: SIRVA and bilateral ankle injuries require medical causation documentation for workers comp claim predicate
If workers comp 'retirement' designation was used to manipulate ERISA plan eligibility (UA342 pension), coordinate ERISA claim with §132a retaliation

case_law.citation: Cabesuela v. Browning-Ferris Industries of California, Inc., 68 Cal.App.4th 101 (1998)
case_law.holding: §132a WCAB jurisdiction is exclusive for workers comp retaliation civil remedies; cannot sue in superior court; but Tameny wrongful discharge tort remains available in superior court
case_law.significance: Established forum boundary between §132a WCAB and superior court Tameny claims

case_law.citation: Tameny v. Atlantic Richfield Co., 27 Cal.3d 167 (1980)
case_law.holding: Tortious wrongful discharge in violation of public policy is a superior court tort claim — allows tort damages (emotional distress, punitive) not available in WCAB §132a proceedings
case_law.significance: Parallel superior court remedy alongside §132a WCAB petition
